issue: Under the third Dunn curtilage factor (how the area was used), should courts consider the homeowner's actual use of the area, or only objective evidence of whether a reasonable officer would view it as used for domestic activities?
provision: U.S. Const. amend. IV; United States v. Dunn, 480 U.S. 294 (1987)

sides.position: Focus on objective evidence: whether a reasonable officer would believe the area was used for domestic activities, not the homeowner's actual use
cases: United States v. Gerard, 362 F.3d 484, 488 (8th Cir. 2004)
United States v. Daughenbaugh, 150 F.3d 594, 599 (court not named in excerpt)
United States v. Moses, 142 F.4th 126 (3d Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Focus on the homeowner's actual use of the area
cases: United States v. Reilly, 76 F.3d 1271, 1278–79 (2d Cir. 1996)
United States v. Diehl, 276 F.3d 32, 40–41 (court not named in excerpt)

quote: Circuits have split over whether to focus on how the homeowner used the area or how it looks objectively to a reasonable officer.
cite: United States v. Ronell Moses, Jr., 142 F.4th 126 (3rd Cir. 2025)
